Flimsy Wire. Up to this point, my main method for slicing blocks of cheese has been a large, stainless steel chef’s knife. It does the job but it’s also a bit awkward and admittedly not ideal. I looked to this cheese slicer as a possible replacement. I would politely describe my experience with it as “disappointing”.

This is a guillotine-style slicer – it has a handle with a thin steel wire that is used to cut through the block when the handle is pressed down, making a clean, straight cut. The surface on which the cheese sits is a nice marble slab with a groove cut in it so that the wire can pass completely through the block without leaving an uncut lip.

In theory this works, and I have seen it work well in other similar slicers. However, for this particular slicer the wire is so flimsy and weak that it bends when slicing and I believe it’s a matter of time (not very long) before it breaks and I have to restring it.

I can’t recommend this slicer. I’ve gone back to using my chef’s knife while I search for better wire to replace the wire that came in this slicer. There are less expensive options that work better.

text:
Almost a Grill Pan. UPDATE 03/10/2018:
I initially rated this pan 3 stars. Having had this pan only about 5 months, large swaths of the Teflon are already coming off, and we've never scrubbed it with anything abrasive or used hard utensils in it. This is a new record (for me) for how quickly the non-stick coating comes off a treated pan. Based on this, I am dropping my rating to 1 star - stay far, far away from this pan. It's a poor product that will fail you sooner rather than later.

My original review follows.

---

I selected this pan for my wife, as she likes to use my cast-iron grill pans but she doesn’t like the clean-up afterward. I will confess that I am no fan of Teflon-coated pans, so I wasn’t too sure about this one. It has turned out to be a decent pan (if you don’t mind Teflon) but there are a couple of negatives that merit attention.

Farberware is not a high-end name in cookware, so I wasn’t expecting this to be a spectacular pan, particularly at the price. I was a bit surprised, though, when I received it – it seems to be very solid with a tightly-attached handle and it is very solidly balanced. This is a big plus, as I have had too many pans that aren’t quite flat on the bottom and as such will wobble on the burner and will heat unevenly. Being aluminum, it heats quickly and because it’s flat it seems to heat evenly. So far, so good.

Some of the other reviewers here have stated that the finish started coming off after the first washing. I have hand-washed this pan several times and so far the finish and the non-stick coating have not shown any signs of coming off. The pan is supposedly dishwasher safe; I have not tried it in the dishwasher so I do not know how well it will hold up in there.

My first issue with this pan is that the ridges aren’t really high enough to make this a proper grill pan. It does leave some grill marks when pre-heated and it does a good job of frying, but it is a poor substitute for most grilling surfaces. Because the ridges are wide and high, it does not grill foods like most other surfaces so the result is something that is more fried than grilled. That said, the ridges are high enough to allow some fats to drain away, so you will end up with moderately lower fat than straight frying, though that depends on how soft and amorphous the food you’re cooking is.

The bottom of the pan is textured and has a neat feel to it, but be careful when running your hand over it. The finer ridges on the bottom aren’t necessarily smooth and I nicked my hand when I ran it across the surface. This was an unpleasant (and unwelcome) surprise. It’s a minor point as most people are not going to make a habit of doing that, but it’s something to remember.

My wife is happy with this pan, though I am not. She has used it several times and it very pleased with how well it works for her and how easy to clean it is. I still prefer my cast iron grill pans and will continue to use them instead, even though cleanup is more work. If the goal is easy cleanup and some fat reduction, this pan is worth a look. If you want a proper grill pan, though, there are better choices available, even in the same general price range.

Very Small and Doesn't Cool Well at All. I selected this mini fridge with one idea in mind - keeping a carton of creamer cold in the office, away from the kitchen so I can always be sure to have creamer for my coffee when I am in the office. I have been sorely disappointed in this unit.

It has two functions, heat and cool. I have little use for the heating function but I have tinkered with it, and it seems to work reasonably well. I have not measured the temperature, but it does keep an open cup of coffee warmer for a longer period of time and it does a reasonable job of working as a cup warmer which is a nice thing if you don't like pouring hot coffee or tea into a cold cup.

The first issue I have with it - and it's a major one - is that it just doesn't get all that cold. It does well enough to give a canned or bottled drink a slight chill but nowhere close to that of a typical refrigerator. This is all right if you don't like drinks that are really cold, but that somewhat defeats the purpose. In this case, a freezer pack in an insulated bag works better for me at cooling a bottled drink down. It is enough to raise some concern in my mind about food safety if leaving anything of consequence in this little fridge for more than a couple of hours. I certainly would not trust an open jar of mayo that was kept in this fridge overnight.

The second problem is that this fridge is too small to accommodate a quart-sized carton of cream, totally defeating the purpose for which I got it. It almost fits, but not quite. This is probably my fault for not measuring, but it's unfortunate nonetheless.

I have real difficulty recommending this little fridge. It's better than nothing I suppose, but there are better options if you're willing to spend a little more.

132Q leaves a LOT to be desired in quality. Please note - this review is for the MACHINE only, and has nothing to do with any particular seller. Seller reviews are in a separate area when you click on the seller. I just want to be clear that this is a PRODUCT review.

I have owned a couple of sewing machines now, and my mother always had Singer machines. I was pleased when I found this one for a very reasonable price, as I wanted to learn to quilt (the "Q" is for quilting on this model). I used it a grand total of four times before it broke. Now, it does a veey nice job, WHEN it works!

I was making pillows when it broke - I had stitched up 2 items, and was on my third. I'd finished the other seams, and was going back over the last seam when it caught and stopped running. Used to bobbins getting linty, I took that apart and blew out any fuzz, and tried the seam again. This time, it caught and I heard a snap. Now the entire machine was frozen up. I couldn't get it to budge, and neither could my husband. He had taken the machine to make sure all the parts were properly greased (they were - after all, it was new). I took the entire bobbin shaft out and made sure there wasn't thread caught where I couldn't see it right away - it was fine.

We took it to a sewing machine repair shop. Apparently, there is a plastic (yes, PLASTIC!!) gear that runs the bobbin gear, and it was stripped out. The thing is, they couldn't find a replacement part for it. We finally took our machine back home, unfixed. So, a grand total of maybe FOUR uses from it before it stopped working. Those are the most expensive pillows I ever made!

Of course, when I wrote to Singer, they gave me a canned reply, stating that if it was within the 90-day warranty (and it wasn't - I'd had it for a few months before I needed to sew anything), then they could help. Otherwise, take it to a repair shop. Gee thanks. This will be my last Singer. Neither the company nor the customer service is what it apparently USED to be. Maybe it is time to try a Brother machine. I also couldn't take it back to the store where I'd purchased it, because I had already used it. It would be dishonest to take it back and say it was broken, when it was working for a short while.

So, save yourself the headaches, and either get a different model, or perhaps consider a different brand. If this is the direction Singer has decided to head for home models - inexpensive low-quality parts in their machines - then choose another brand. They might also be made with lots of plastic, but it won't cost what the Singer machines cost.

UPDATE: We did order replacement parts and were able to get metal to replace the plastic. This is how Singer should have done it in the first place! I went to set it up to try and sew with it. The first thing that happened? I picked it up by the handle, and the handle fell off! OMG - this is the CHEAPEST sewing machine ever! Please save your money and buy a different model! And now I need to make another trip to buy a bobbin case, because apparently, it was removed during the repair. Went to load the bobbin and no case! One headache after another. This was my last Singer. The missing bobbin case is not Singer's fault, but everything else is. They did not reimburse me for the cost of replacing the part, despite it breaking on the first use. They offered nothing - no replacement parts, no courtesy doodad, not even concern. They've gone way downhill in the home machine line.)

You still need a liner! This won't do the job alone. Well, the mystery of how my daughter flooded our bathroom floor has been solved.

I bought this liner (clearly marked LINER, note) to go with a new fabric shower curtain
I had also purchased. Previously, we had just a vinyl curtain only. We have your basic bathtub - nothing
special or oversized, and we hung the liner and curtain like we always have.

First, the positives -
this curtain is beautiful - it really is. It has a light striped effect in shades of beige,
and it looks great on the hooks. It is very well made, and the weights in the bottom are exactly
what we had been looking for to keep the liner from billowing up and sticking to our soapy selves.
This is hanging on the INside of the tub, as liners should, with the new curtain on the outside of the tub.

After the first shower with the new curtains in place, we had a soaked floor, soaked rugs, etc.
We couldn't figure out what she did, and thought maybe water was hitting shampoo bottles and "leaking" out that way.
We even had blamed her for being careless with the handheld shower head.
Then I took a shower this morning.

I, too, had a flooded bathroom floor from a 10-12 minute shower. What the heck?!
I had made doubly sure that the corners/edges of the tub were covered with the liner.
Then I noticed what was really going on -

THIS LINER IS NOT WATERPROOF!
Nope - at least mine isn't!

This beautiful shower curtain "liner" should be considered a curtain ONLY.
It does not even repel water! It keeps shower spray in for a short while, but if water bounces off you and on to
the curtain, or you aim your shower head at the curtain to rinse off some soap, you will have
a soaked floor. This does NOT act like a liner at all, and in fact creates a wet mess.

Now, I know it said this was a fabric shower curtain liner, but wouldn't you think if it states
it is a LINER that it would be waterproof?!? I know I sure did! But it isn't.
At the end of my relatively short shower, my liner was soaked through, and had several places of
my new separate actual shower curtain soaked as well, and water puddled on the floor from where it dripped down
off the soaked fabric shower curtain. My rugs were soaked, as was a cardboard box of cat food packets I'd sat
on the floor, waiting to be put in the cupboard.

I've already discarded the packaging or I would return it. This is pitiful!
I like how the weights keep the curtain down in the tub, so my plan is to get a REAL liner that is
actually waterproof, and add it to the rings INBETWEEN the new curtain and this fabric liner.

Seriously - this was so disappointing! I really thought anything that called itself a liner
would act like one, but I was very wrong. I gave it two stars ONLY because it is very well made.

I would advise anyone thinking about getting this item (in any color) that they should consider it to be
ONLY a curtain, and to use a vinyl liner of some sort with it. It will keep someone from seeing you
"nekkid", but that is all it will do. It is not water repellant or water proof.

Just goes to show you that beauty does not mean brains - this looks a lot better than it works!

Very glad we bought it at the time. I wasn't really sure what to expect with this little heater.
We have an upstairs bedroom in a rental place (where we can't do major changes), and it
is very chilly in the winter. Add wind, and it gets freaky cold inside! We've actually had
ice on the closet walls before.

So, I wanted to get a small space heater that wouldn't require us running the central heat
if only our bedroom was cold.

This little guy does the job very well.
I don't find the noise annoying - it is like a computer running, with slight magnification.
It is not as noisy as a fan. I don't mind it a bit, and it can be like white noise, blocking
out other small annoyances.

This is so completely adjustable, it makes it great.
I've used both the high and low power settings, and don't see a huge difference between them.
I guess the high technically heats up faster, but again, I didn't really notice.
The other dial is how warm you want the air to be that comes out.
I've used it on many of the settings so far. Yesterday, for example, had 30-40 mph winds here
and it was very cold in the bedroom - cold enough I had a hard time sewing something by hand!
I put the little heater aimed at my desk, and within 1/2 hr, the room was very comfortable.
The room is about 12' x 10'. By the time my daughter got home from school, it was too hot,
and we had to turn it off for a while!

All in all, I'm very happy with it. We bought two different kinds, one for downstairs and one
for upstairs, to try to cut back on our utility bill. The other brand works just fine too, but
I think this one is a little better! : )

All in all, I would definitely recommend it. It won't heat a 2-story house, but it does 2 or 3 rooms
to a pleasant temperature (I don't like it super hot anyway, but it gets to 72 pretty easily) very well.
Upstairs, we have two bedrooms and a small bathroom. I can put this in the hallway, and, although it
takes a little longer, will have the upstairs comfortably warm in an hour or so. The bedroom alone
with the heater in the room takes much less time. I've even had it near the desk when my hands
were freezing while typing!

Not sure how great the fan alone will be - I'll try that when it gets stuffy some day.
But I bought it for heating, and it does exactly what it says, and does it well.
Very pleased with the purchase.

=============================================================
UPDATE:

Well, we had our first problem with the heater today!
We have used it probably ten times this winter, and it has done a wonderful job of warming
the bedroom/hall area. HOWEVER - today, March 29, we went to unplug the heater and box it
back up for next winter's use. This is where the problem began!

I tried to unplug the heater, and couldn't do it! I tried and failed, tried the other hand and failed.
When my son got home, had HIM try and he failed! It took the two of us to get the heater disconnected
from the plug, and when we finally did, the prongs came out of the plug!! OMG.
Well, THAT was an interesting development!

I checked on the website, and the heater has a one-year warranty on parts. So, I contacted
Lasko via their customer care center, and we'll see what they will do about it!
I could hardly believe it! We've had it plugged in since December, so around three months,
but I really don't think that's long enough to create a stuck plug problem!
I'll update about how Lasko customer service is once I hear back, and we find a resolution to the problem.

Until then - unplug carefully! You can see the glue on the end of the plug on ours!

UPDATE:
No response from Lasko yet, so it is looking like I'll be buying another brand
of small space heater for next winter. What a shame. I really did like this one.
My husband has another brand, however, that did equally well at heating the room.
Lasko isn't the only player in the game at this point. Disappointing on the customer service
oversight. I've had it too long to ask Amazon to handle the problem - it isn't their fault
the plug was faulty - but sure wish I could send it back for a replacement!
I am dinging it one star both because of the plug, and because of the lack of support over
a product that was only a few months old and allegedly still under warranty.

UPDATE OCT 2013:
Here it is, late 2013, and Lasko never bothered to respond to our concerns.
The heater has been sitting in the hallway since the plug pulled out several months ago.
Now that winter is getting closer again, I am back on Amazon, looking for another heater.
It will NOT be this one - it worked like a champ, UNTIL we needed to unplug it!
Note that it is STILL UNDER WARRANTY, and they won't respond to the problem.

What the worst part was was Lasko ignoring our request entirely. No replacement heater,
replacement cord, credit towards another one, nothing at all.
So, we will be looking at other brands. Most have similar wattages now, so there is no
reason to be brand loyal, when they didn't care a bit about us.

DO NOT BELIEVE THE HYPE OR THE CLAIMS. Editing my initial review (which is still below this revision), on September 16, 2013: So, the description here at Amazon for this vacuum has been changed from "NO MESS" to "LESS MESS." Much better description, as there is plenty of mess to clean up inside the vacuum dirt collection tray area. Also, a price drop, from $350 to $299.95. Over at Brookstone's Website, the "NO MESS" description has also been removed and changed to "Less Mess." I feel the fact the "NO MESS" description has been removed validates my original review. And I thank Brookstone for coming clean (no pun intended). And for those who accused me of lacking credibility with my review because it doesn't say "Amazon Verified Purchase," I'd like to reiterate here that I purchased this vacuum direct from Brookstone and not here at Amazon because at the time of purchase Brookstone had a coupon available, which lowered the price for me a bit. I still own and use the vacuum.

Original Review:

This vacuum (at $350) is so overpriced, it is insane.

First, let me warn you: Should your $350 Gtech Airram's battery ever fail, there is no way to use the vacuum. It would just be a brick. For that much money, they should allow, just as an emergency backup, the vacuum to be used with the charging cable plugged in. But no. If the battery is drained or dead, even with the cord plugged into it, the vacuum is useless.

But the above is not why I give this vacuum 2 stars.

They claim no mess? There is mess. In fact, you might need another vacuum to clean out the mess (dirt and dust and stuff vacuumed up) that accumulates into the collection area (even immediately after first use). Yes you will! (Yes, you can grab a cloth and wipe out all that dust. You will want to and have to. The video showing how the collection area has no mess, along with the written claims of same, are utter bs.)

I bought this vacuum direct from Brookstone, and am very disappointed. I really thought that for $350, there would be no mess (or at least, a tiny amount). One big complaint about bagless vacs is the mess in the collection areas. So, Gtech, in an effort to make the cost so high, claims "lightweight, clean, and cordless...no mess." It is lightweight. It is cordless. But it ain't clean. Not in the least. And there is mess.

So, if you got a lot of extra money to spend and you want cordless, light, and powerful, buy this vacuum. But do not expect clean. The only thing "clean" about this vac is that after you open up the cover, you're gonna have to CLEAN the inside.

To summarize: This vacuum is in no way worth $350, in my opinion...and you will have to clean the dust and dirt out of the collection area (with a rag or paper towels) just like you would with any bagless. There is mess and particles to manually empty seperate from what they call the "bales of dirt." Their so called "bales" after pulled out, stuff is still stuck to the underside of the cover, which you will have to pick out with your fingers. (This vacuum is not worth anything over $180, in my opinion.)

I Love the "Bagged Cordless Vac" Concept -- Very Unhappy With The Attachments. As of the posting of this review, the cost for this vacuum here and at Oreck is $569.99. That's quite a premium for the wonderful new concept of making this kind of cordless hand vacuum with a bag (they call them "Pods") rather than the always messy and dirty and dusty collection containers. (I am surprised it took this long for someone to invent a "bagged" cordless hand vacuum...and bravo to Oreck for being the first to do it. Yes, one has to buy the replacement Pods--Oreck includes 5 with the vacuum--but they're only $15 for a 5-pack.)

While I love the bagged-cordless concept, I was disappointed with this vacuum overall, mostly having to do with attachments to be used when using it has a hand-held, and with its heavy weight, which can make it feel a bit uncomfortable rather quickly for those who are not as strong as some. (Please keep in mind that my primary use for this Oreck vac is as a handheld, and not for use as a floor vac.)

The worst attachment by far is the "Soft-Bristle Dust Brush tool. The black bristles shed immediately upon first use, and shed very badly. (And the first use was just over soft bed sheets.) The soft bristles have stretched outward/become deformed in several places, as well, and just won't stop shedding.

The second worst attachment is the small "AirPower Pivoting Brushroll Tool." The vacuum stops working when using this tool way too often and way too easily, where a red light comes on, as if the vacuum thinks the suction is being blocked. And I assure you I am not applying too much pressure when using this tool.

The Crevice Tool works as it should, but because the two release buttons are so far back, it is not the easiest to eject the tool right away, on the first attempt.

I do like that one does not have to hold the power button down for this to work. Turn the dial to power it on, and it stays on.

Suction in low power mode is a bit weak, but adequate for some easy-to-vacuum-up stuff. Suction in high power mode, which will make the battery power drain faster, of course, is very good.

And finally, I am disappointed they could not make this vacuum work while the a/c cord is plugged in charging the battery. This would have been a great emergency backup if the battery was dead and you wanted to still use this vacuum. But no, when the the electrical cord is plugged in, the vacuum will not turn on.

Edit 8-29-2018: Oreck sent me a 2nd soft bristle dust brush. And after I reported that that brush also shed and had deformed bristles they sent a 3rd. The 3rd brush also immediately shed quite badly just by very gently rubbing the brush over very soft material.

Another Love-Hate Relationship With A Dyson Vacuum. Should Be Different For Its High Price. I bought the V6 Absolute cheaper elsewhere, and not here via Amazon.

There are two suction levels: Low and Max. There is a remarkable difference between the suction power between the two. If you doubt this, simply attach the dust brush and hold it at the bottom of your shirt. On low, your shirt will not be held on by the suction. On Max, your shirt will be held onto the suction quite nicely, and as you'd expect.

I am extremely disappointed by the low suction power when the vacuum is not on the Max setting, I do not wanna use it. It just is not good enough. But on the vastly superior Max setting, you get a measly 6-minutes of battery power.

For its high price Dyson could have rectified this situation by designing the vac with a removable battery, and then include a second battery you can keep charged. When your 6 minutes are up, simply swap the second battery...putting the first battery into a charger.

Also, disappointingly, you cannot use this vacuum while the battery is being charged. This might have been a helpful feature if one ran out of battery after the 6 minutes but really needed to finish up a job right away.

For this whopping price, to only get 6 minutes using the desired Max suction setting is extremely upsetting to me. Again, I find the low setting suction level to be way to weak.

I realize battery technology is still limited...which is why I suggested they could have made this vacuum be able to swap out the battery, etc.

I do love the soft roller brush. I do love the handling of the vacuum. I do love the suction when it is on Max (and only on Max). Filter cleaning is easy. So, like I said, Love/Hate.

Again, this is a vacuum that they MSRP'd and originally sold it at their site for $599. Right now, as I write this review, they discounted it to $479.99. That is a lot of money for just 6 minutes of battery life for the suction I expect and the suction power I want. (And they could have easily fixed this situation by designing it with a swap-able battery, and including a second battery.)

On a side note: Hopefully one day Dyson will make a Cinetic cordless that has no filters to clean, just like with their wonderful Cinetic Big Ball Animal + Allergy. Once Dyson can give us a Cinetic Cordless with no filters to clean and more than 6 minutes of battery life on Max suction setting...my feelings will go from Love/Hate, to just Love.

Message To Panasonic: Stop Putting On Tape That Leaves Marks!. I am rating this one star in the hope that someone at Panasonic will read this. It is inexcusable to put tape on Stainless Steel (or anything) that is going to leave a noticeable blemish or mark or discoloration when removed! Why would you do this?

So, Panasonic puts two separate long pieces of tape to hold the door closed during shipping. When I carefully and slowly peeled this tape off, it left behind discolorations...and I mean large and noticeable discolorations where the tape was. I tried washing it...and while it faded a bit, the discolorations/blemishes remain. This is infuriating to me. An expensive and very nice looking microwave marred because they choose to put crap tape on the stainless steel to hold the door closed.

I hate it! And Amazon "One Star" means "I Hate It." So, that justifies my one-star rating.

I am going to keep the microwave because I fear replacing it will end up with the same result. I have the sensor placed just below the rail right about where it is supposed to be under your chest and above the hinged area of the platform.
Initial setup was fairly straightforward. After collecting several days worth of data I decided to delete them just because I was trying out features. Somehow deleting all sleep data caused the app to malfunction and close the moment it was started. I had to delete the app, reinstall and reregister everything. That took a few tries. Several days later the cable was accidentally unplugged from the adapter. I went through the setup procedure, nothing, several times. I read the help file and found out how to do a factory reset. I had to perform this seven times before the app would connect to the sensor again. I used the device for another week and suddenly it stopped collecting sleep data. For four days it sat under my mattress doing nothing. I tried contacting support and have not received a reply yet. An earlier question was answered fairly quick but I had to provide the serial number (adding a full day to the exchange) to get a simple data meaning question answered. On the fifth day the unit once again began sending data to the app. Is it defective? Perhaps. I'm unsure. But that leads me to my deepest concern. . .
I don't trust the veracity of the data collected. It's supposed to be able to tell how long it takes you to fall asleep, when you're lightly or deeply asleep or in REM sleep as well as tracking when you snore, your pulse rate high, low and average through the night and how long it takes you to get up when you awake. I was impressed with all these bar graphs and data until I started looking closely. Every night I go to bed early due to pain and will spend up to a few hours reading or watching video on my tablet. when the bar graph said I was lightly asleep, I wasn't. When it said I was deeply asleep, I wasn't. I have no idea how, without seeing my eye movement, it can know I'm in REM sleep. I think one time it said I took a while to get to sleep but most nights while I lay there reading it was logging it as some form of sleep and my falling asleep taking only a few minutes. I know I snore, my scouts once dragged me out of the tent because I was so loud, so I guess the snoring detector is accurate. It can also, some times, tell if you've taken a nap during the day and add that to the day's data though it appears there needs to be a susstantial time between getting up and going back for a nap otherwise the time gap gets logged as simply a really long interuption in your night's sleep. I tend to spend quite some time in bed on bad days and that seems to seriously confuse the device and app.
It's a slick idea, nothing to wear, nothing to start or stop manually. Just stuff it under your mattress as directed and hey presto, sleep data. Too bad it's dreadfully inaccurate has connection issues and stops and starts recording data for no good reason. It would be great if it were even 80% accurate but I know for a fact it's no where near.

text:
Digital read-out is gradually dying. Otherwise it would be a great product.. I purchased one of these units in January 2014. As stated in other reviews, the accompanying pan is made of rather thin stainless steel, which does limit it's usefulness. On a low heat setting, I have successfully cooked curries, braised meats, etc. However, on a high heat setting everything burns and everything sticks. But I've since bought a fairly cheap set of nicely made and induction-friendly Cuisinart pans from Costco ($200 for an impressive 13 piece set) which work beautifully on this unit.

However, the main reason I'm writing this review today is that from about 6 months after beginning to use this unit, the LED digital display has slowly deteriorated, bar by bar, until 10 looks like "1]", 8=9, 6=5, and the 2 looks something like "?". I only use the heat level settings, rarely specific temperature, but I think that would be even harder to decipher now.

The rest of the unit works fine, but the manufacturer needs to find a better source for the display components. There's really no excuse for faulty LEDs. Eventually, I expect, the readout will be so bad that it will render the whole thing useless. I should have sent it back when it first started to go bad.

Prettiest hunk of plastic junk I've ever owned.. My wife picked up this Bissell on sale at a local store, we needed a new vacuum and wanted a bagless model that "specialized" in pet hair. What we got was a complete waste of money (nobody listens to me when I say do a little research first). There isn't one thing this vacuum does well - not one! I could say that the candy apple red paint is a nice touch...but I buy vacuums to clean my house, not to look nice when I open the hall closet.

If you like a LOUD vacuum with the suction power of TWO drinking straws, this is the vacuum for you. I think Bissell says in the manual that you have to remove the insert above the canister and clean it every once in awhile. We have one dog and one cat, and have to remove that insert about 2-3 times a month. This isn't a 'bang around the trash can' cleanout, either; I have to take it into the garage and blow it out with the air compressor. Do YOU have a compressor in your garage? There's so many nooks and crannies in the insert that it's pretty much a requirement to blow it out to clear the air passages. I know, I know...the engineers didn't expect this thing to be moving DUSTY AIR through its MULTI CYCLONIC SYSTEM.

That pet brush you see up on the handle? That is a junk extension of a junk device. It falls off at the slightest tap of the main vacuum chassis, and stopped working after 3 uses (you could hear the high-quality plastic bearings making noise during the first use). Right now it lives in the bottom of the closet, because it's useless and just falls off anyway.

There is another brush head on the body of the removable canister, which falls off 50% less than the pet brush. This one actually collects the pet hair so you can pick it out by hand and spoon-feed it to the vacuum. In fact, you'll be hand-feeding this hunk of crap more than you think - it needs a LOT of help. Find any hair/crumbs/glitter/anything on your carpet? You'll be making at least two passes before Ol' Faithful even considers picking it up...and then you stand a good chance of the offending item getting dropped out of the vacuum head as soon as you turn it off. It doesn't even pick up pet hair, which is what seems to be a selling point judging by all the dumb stickers on this thing. It's like an auto body guy from NASCAR works in Bissell's marketing department - STICKERS EVERYWHERE.

The hose itself is pretty inflexible and just about long enough, and the hose extension is another quality design by those Bissell MBAs...I mean, engineers. The extension has a twist lock in the middle, which will crack after maybe 6 months of use...rendering it useless as well. I've checked multiple times, and there are no blockages in any passageways; this thing is just very poorly designed.

Overall, keep looking right past this thing. It may look nice, but that's about it.

F+ -->What was Bissell thinking?. I have a Bissell Spot Bot and I purchased a Bissell 9400 ProHeat 2X Select Upright Deep Carpet Cleaner for my boyfriend; both are superb products! However, I cannot phathom what Bissell was thinking when they produced this carpet cleaner. I tried it on an area of carpet that was only slightly dirty; but the results were very disappointing.

What they got right:
- Easy assembly
- Sleek vacuum design
- Useable power tools (power nozzle is good)
- Easy carry handle
- Excellent power cord holder
- Nice power cord release mechanism (no need to unwind cord from power cord wrap because you can just release the latch to drop the cord to the floor)
- Vacuum powers itself nicely along the carpet so there is hardly any pushing action required by the user

What they got terribly wrong:
- The soft PowerRoller doesn't clean; it's excellent on hardwood floors but that is not what this vacuum was designed for.
- The carpet does not dry in 30 minutes as stated UNLESS you hardly use any solution. Without using much solution, you might as well blow on the carpet with your mouth to try to dislodge the dirt because the results would probably be the same--which is no cleaning.
- The solution tank leaks around the cap when filled appropriately. I tried several times to reseal the cap but there was always some solution seepage.
- The dirty water collector tank also has water seepage even if you don't go above the fill line.
- I tried for 45 minutes to clean about a 6 x 7 area of carpet and it still looked as dirty as when I started. I then used the power tool and some elbow grease and tried again which gave me better results but still not good enough. My Bissell spot bot can clean the same area wonderfully but not this vacuum.
- By the time the hot water reaches the carpet it is either lukewarm or too cold to be of any cleaning use.

In summary, if the Bissell didn't leak all over, this vacuum would be excellent (but perhaps overkill) for cleaning a wood floor because the cleaning pad buffs up things nicely (I tried it my wood floor). However as a carpet cleaner, you would get better results by wetting a washcloth with warm water, applying some soap, getting down on your hands and knees and using some elbow grease to clean your carpet.

Decent vacuum for those who don't have pets or allergies but not for me. My first impression of this vacuum was that it was a four-star product. However after a full evaluation, in my opinion this is a three-star vacuum for non-pet owners and those without allergies. Although this Bissell has a lot of PROS, it is a two-star vacuum for my purposes because I have pets and allergies to dust.

PROS:
- Easy and intuitive assembly without reading manual (requires long Phillips screwdriver to tighten screw in handle which is a little awkward to tighten in the long hole)
- Incredible suction
- All tools fit snugly into their holders on the vacuum
- The Model 58F8-3 comes with a combination dusting brush/upholstery tool, a crevice tool, extension wand, and TurboBrush
- Retractable cord
- No need to purchase bags
- Has a bright headlight
- The internal filter is washable; all except for the HEPA Media Filter which has to be replaced
- Vacuum components are easy to disassemble without tools except for the headlight and drive belt replacement
- 25-ft power cord (according to the product description online; but this is not mentioned in the manual)
- Height adjustment knobs and other controls such as on/off switch and handle release pedal as easy to operate and locate
- Easy to empty dirt container and remove filter cup
- Has clean filter indicator and clean carpet sensor
- Vacuum has a three-year limited warranty

CONS:
- Vacuum was difficult to maneuver due to incredible suction
- Vacuum is very loud
- If the hose falls out of the hose wand base during vacuuming, a lot of dust escapes through the hole filing the house in a cloud
- Hair from pets clogged the filter cup even before the filter cup was full rendering the turbo brush in operable until everything was cleaned out
- Filter indicator light didn't change to red even though I had to clean out the filter cup
- The clean carpet sensors did not appear reliable to me. Many times it would show a steady green to indicate the carpet was clean, then it would turn to red when I went over the same carpet again and again; yet the carpet was clean.
- Emptying the filter cup and cleaning the filter was VERY MESSY
- Instructions don't give any recommendationos on when you should wash or replace filters
- I don't understand the meaning of a HEPA filter when so much dust escapes the vacuum if the hose falls out of the wand base or when emptying the filter cup
- The floor brush continues to rotate when you use the vacuum attachments which could wear out your carpet or mark up your floor while you are using the tools with the hose.
- I would have liked a cord that was about 2-3 feet longer

My arm hurt after using this vacuum because no matter how I changed the height adjustment knob, the Bissell required a lot force to push around. I was actually sweating after I vacuumed my rug. Also, the pet hair I picked up got caught in the upper filter area requiring a cup cleaning and filter shaking before the filter cup was full. In addition, the filter emptying process (although very, very easy) was incredibly messy. By the time I was done, I had to re-vacuum the area where I emptied the filter cup. In addition, there was a cloud of dust around my house similar to the type of dust kicked up by a Shop Vac. Of course, I used a carpet powder on my rug which only exacerbated the problem. I also didn't like how the floor brush on the upright continues to rotate while I was using the wand tools. To me this was unnessary and could result in excess wear on my carpet or scratch my floors.

In summary, this vacuum does pick up a lot of dirt and is easily assembled, which is excellent. Its interesting features are average. However, I can't recommend this vacuum for someone who has pets or has allergies to dust for the above reasons. Instead, I recommend buying a vacuum with a bag that isn't so loud or so messy to clean.

text:
Beautiful to look at but with some design flaws. This is a gorgeous little tea kettle and is much smaller than I expected. This kettle is only for heating up water and nothing else. Below are the PROS and CONS including some design flaws.

PROS
- The unit is so pretty to me.
- There are five temperature settings - 212 (best for black and pu-erh teas and tisanes such as rooibos and herbal teas), 195 (best for oolong teas and some herbal teas; can be used for yellow teas if left to cool slightly), 175 (best for white teas), and 160 (best for green teas although I brew these teas around 175). The fifth setting is for 100 degrees to keep the water warm.
- Cord storage is hidden underneath the unit.
- The kettle fits nicely into the base as long as you line up the matching dots correctly.
- I like the push button feature of the dial to turn on the unit and the blue light on the dial.
- The lid on the carafe snaps nicely into place.
- It reaches the desired temperature pretty fast.
- Anywhere between 16 ounces and 48 ounces (2-8 cups) of water can be heated.

CONS:
- There are no in-between temperature settings; it must be dialed into 212, 195, 175, and 160 for brewing or 100 for keeping the water warm.
- There is no audible signal to tell you when the water has reached its desired temperature; the only way to tell is to watch the light go out. To me this is a design flaw because now I have to watch the water reach its temperature and there's no "automatic keep warm" feature.
- The lid is difficult snap into the upright position when there's hot water in the carafe.
- The neck of the carafe is so tiny that it is impossible to get a hand in the carafe to dry the inside unless your hand is small. I am able to get my hand inside when I am not using a towel; but as soon as I introduce a towel it's impossible for me.
- The other design flaw is that when there are 16 ounces of water in the kettle, the unit feels hotter to me and it was almost impossible not to burn myself when pouring the water because of the steam and heat emanating from the top of the unit. Of course, wearing an oven mitt or holding a towel will prevent this possibility.
- The lid is not removable.
- At the current price of $79.99, I think this is too expensive a purchase for what you are getting.

It is important to read the manual for this unit. For instance, the carafe has to be seated correctly before turning on the unit or the power light will blink and the unit will not work.

This unit should not be washed because all components, including the carafe, are electric. Only dry the inside and wipe down with a damp cloth. Although this Capresso does the job it is supposed to do, the two design flaws that made me rate this 2 stars instead of 3 was that there was no audible signal to tell you when the water is heated to the desired temperature and the fact that the water is too hot to pour when boiling unless using a mitt or towel to hold the very hot carafe. Other than this this is an average kettle. I cannot vouch for its longevity as I've only heated water 4 times in this unit so far. I will post an update if things change. If this unit were priced in the $29 range, I would have given it 3 stars despite its flaws.

If you are a real tea connoisseur, it is better to pay $170 more for the [[ASIN:B003LNOPSG Breville BTM800XL One-Touch Tea Maker]]. I personally purchased and own two of these. If you only make teas with boiling water and want to make tea for company, then you might consider the [[ASIN:B007UEEJVK Nesco TM-1 Teamaker, 1-Liter]]. I also own this one and although it is average, at least you can make tea in it. I've attached my reviews to the other tea makers in the comment section of this review for those who are interested.

In summary, I would pass on this Capresso.

Update November 2013 - This kettle stopped working so now it's headed for the garbage. This is not the life expectancy I would expect and had I purchased it I would be very disappointed.

I am really impressed with this soap dispensing sink brush. It fact it is the best I ever tried but I only started using it so time will tell.

WHAT I LIKE

- This is so easy to fill. I just lightly pulled up the plug in the handle to fill it with dish detergent and then pressed down to seal the plug in place.

- One push on the center button and a 5 to 25-cent-sized dollop of soap is dispensed.

- The handle is long and has a nice grip for ease of use.

- The brush bristles are slightly stiff for moderate cleaning.

- The brush head is removable by twisting it to the left to dislodge.

- There's a scraper on the underside of the brush; it's not something I would likely use but it's nice to know it's there if needed.

- The brush comes with a limited lifetime warranty but one has to pay to ship the brush back to them for a replacement.

WHAT I DISLIKE

Bare bones almost powerless cordless vacuum; picks up light dust and wisps of hair only. I am very disappointed in this cordless vacuum because it lacks any “pick-me-up.” I was only able to pick up tiny wisps of cat hair and dust and was barely able to pick up any cat litter sprinkled throughout the carpet or bare floor. If I uncoupled the hand vac from the floor head, then it had a bit more suction but still not enough. However, there is no way I am vacuuming a floor on my hands and knees with a hand vac even if the suction were great. This vacuum is too weak to be useful to me.

FACTS:

- Assembly of the four parts (floor head, hand vac, extension pole, top curved handle) is required.

- The fifth part is the charging cord that plugs into the hand vac portion of the vacuum.

- The floor head has no beater bar (meaning no rotating brush).

- There is no charging light on the vacuum or the charging cord.

- A charge of 16 hours before first use is needed and it is safe to leave on the charger indefinitely.

- The curved handle and pole are not removable once assembled; however, rest of vacuum comes apart for configuring into the various combinations.

- This is a 4-in-1 vacuum meaning there are four vacuum component combinations:
1) with floor head and hand vac attached (short handle)
2) with just the hand vac (meaning no floor head or pole handle)
3) with just the hand vac and long pole handle
4) with floor head and long handle attached to the hand vac – note that this is the typical upright full vacuum.

LIKES:

- Self-standing design with ability to hang from handle hole as well. There is also a wall fitting available for purchase according to the instructions in case one wants to hang the vacuum on the wall.

- Dust bowl and filter are easy to empty and wash.

- Swivel steering.

- "Ease of glide" along my bare floor.

- Two-year limited warranty

- Cordless with lithium ion battery (wall charger cord included)

DISLIKES in order of importance to me:

- There is limited suction, especially when fully assembled as an upright vacuum.

- The vacuum feels cheap like the plastic will break after a while.

- The floor head and hand vac are difficult to couple and uncouple.

- There is no charging light.

- The assembly instructions are not clear when it comes which way to line up the holes in the handle.

In summary, this is truly a bare bones vacuum. To get four stars, it would have to be able to pick up the tiny granules of cat litter sprinkled throughout my floor and carpet. To get five stars it would also have to feel sturdier than it currently feels.

Brews a good cup of tea but so many steps & a separate timer are needed; NOT worth it. I am a tea connoisseur that loves loose leaf teas to be brewed correctly and at the right temperature. Unless one brews only black or pu-erh tea or herbal tisanes, then a brewer that brews at different temperatures is required in order to extract the correct flavor profile of that tea. This is where this Breville BTM500 Smart Tea Infuser is supposed to shine. After having tried this brewer, it does brew the tea correctly but it is so cumbersome to use and there are so many steps involved that it is not worth the price, in my opinion.

Before I go into the PROs and CONS of this particular teapot, I want to explain a little bit about the tools I use now to brew tea.

My favorite pot is a [[ASIN:B003LNOPSG Breville One-Touch Tea Maker]]. I originally purchased one of those at $250 and then purchased a second one for $199.99 because I felt I could not live without it if the first one broke. It is is the only tea brewer I know of that does a phenomenal job of brewing tea that is to be enjoyed to the last drip and brews with the least hassle. However, if I only want one cup of tea, I use the much simpler [[ASIN:B00DHLAC66 Frigidaire Professional Programmable Water Kettle]] to heat water to the correct temperature for one cup of tea.

I also occasionally use a tea kettle to just boil water to brew one cup of black tea with a tea infuser. When I want more than one cup of black tea, I use the [[ASIN:B007UEEJVK Nesco TM-1 Teamaker, 1-Liter]] which acts like a coffee pot but for tea and only brews with boiling water.

Although this Smart Tea Infuser does produce a high quality brew, there is just not enough good about it compared to the bad.

WHAT I LOVE:
- It brews a good cup of tea of varying kinds at the appropriate temperatures.

- Water can be boiled in this.

- There is a cord storage underneath the base.

- This is an attractive tea maker that looks great on my counter top.

WHAT I DISLIKE (in order of my biggest hate):
- Brewing the tea requires several steps. First the kettle needs to be filled with the desired amount of water. Second, the lid rim and top need to be inserted. Third, the tea type / temperature need to be selected. Then the unit needs to be turned on (a.k.a. started). Fourth, once the unit beeps (which takes several long minutes), the tea basket has to be inserted with the correct amount of tea. Fifth, the steeping time has to be set and then the START TIMER button pressed to start steeping. However, there is no light on that button to indicate it was even pressed. Once the cycle is complete, the tea maker is supposed to beep three times. I was unable to get it to beep. This means I now have to time how long I am steeping it for with a separate timer or sit and watch until the other lights on the pot go out. Now the tea can be enjoyed but it is important to remove the tea basket first so it does not over steep. After the tea is poured, I have to follow more steps to keep it warm. I have to return the tea kettle to power base and press and hold the TEMP / KEEP WARM button for two seconds. This will keep the tea warm for 30 minutes unless I remove the kettle, after which I have to reset.

- The long brew basket makes it difficult to remove the spent leaves from the basket.

- The unit does not remember the last settings chosen after a power off.

- Custom programming is not possible as there is only a set selection of temperatures.

- There is no auto start option. This means one cannot wake up to a freshly brewed cup of tea. For the price of this unit, I would have expected this.

- The current cost of $149 is way too expensive for the cumbersome features of this brewer. I recommend spending $50 more to buy the [[ASIN:B003LNOPSG Breville One-Touch Tea Maker]]. Perhaps this is Breville's way of getting people to buy their one touch by making a substandard tea infuser.

- There is no secondary strainer at the spout of the carafe to catch any wayward leaves from escaping into my cup; although, this is unlikely given the tight "weave" of the brew basket.

- The base (obviously) and the carafe itself (that needs special care of wiping down or rinsing gently inside only) cannot be washed. This is the same with their one-touch tea maker.

MORE DISAPPOINTMENTS
- The quick start guide and instruction manual contradict each other. The quick start guide says to leave the tea basket in when cleaning for first use; the instruction manual says to remove it. The quick start guides forgets to tell you about selecting the steep time and has you just starting the timer.

- The instruction manual contains erroneous tea information. Most tea is oxidized (exposed to air) and not fermented (converted via use of microbes). Although some use those words interchangeably, they do not mean the same thing and there is a lot of misinformation out in the tea world about this.

In summary, this is definitely not worth the purchase. There are entirely too many steps required to achieve the perfect brew. The tea basket is too long and narrow which makes it difficult to empty. In addition, the unit does not beep three times when the steeping time is over as the manual says. If you just love different loose leaf teas and want to experience the various subtleties in the liquor of these different brews, then save for the [[ASIN:B003LNOPSG Breville One-Touch Tea Maker]] because that tea maker is worth it and this one does not even come close.

Low quality, low-end cookware. This is a 14-piece non-stick aluminum set that includes:

One 5 qt / 4.75 L Covered Dutch Oven
One 2 qt / 1.9 L Covered Saucepan
One 1 qt / 0.95L Covered Saucepan
One 10.25 in / 26 cm Covered Fry Pan (has Thermo-Spot heat indicator)
One 8 in / 20 cm Fry Pan (has Thermo-Spot heat indicator)
One "One Egg Wonder"
4 Plastic Measuring Spoons

The package states these pots have a safe non-stick coating with NO PFOA, NO LEAD, and NO Cadmium. It also indicates that the set can be used on a gas, coil/solid electric, ceramic, or halogen stove. It is made in China and comes with a limited lifetime warranty. I tested my set on a gas stove.

What I like about this set is that it has a large covered fry pan. Most fry pans do not have covers. I also like the brick red color, the handles on the pots, and the tops on the lids which are easy to grip. The pots also wash well. However, I dislike a lot about this cookware.

- The lids do not fit snugly on the large pot or fry pan because the pans are sort of misshaped (not fully circular) causing a gap. The two saucepan covers fit snugly, however.

- The cookware does not hold heat well.

- The 1 qt saucepan easily tips just by touching the handle unless the contents inside are heavy.

- I saw no change in the Thermo- Spot heat indicator of the two fry pans even after heating them up for 5 minutes; so that feature does not work.

- The package says this is oven safe up to 350 degrees (177 C). Personally that is useless to me because I cook at 350 or above. Since many oven temperatures are not exact, it would be easy to go over 350 and the handles would most likely be destroyed.

- For those who use a dishwasher, it says dishwasher safe on the box but the instructions say hand washing is recommended for the non-stick pots.

- The egg I cooked stuck to the non-stick coating of the "one egg wonder" although it did clean up pretty well after soaking.

- The pots also do not stack well because they slip around a lot.

As a side note, since the pots have a non-stick coating, those with pet birds have to be careful using this around them or they could die from the toxicity. The fumes the heated non-stick coating gives off are toxic to birds.

Had I purchased this cookware I would have been extremely upset and sent it back for a refund. This set is just barely serviceable and I cannot recommend this cookware. It is both low end and low quality in my opinion. In fact, I am stunned that others find this cookware favorable to them.

This denim apron gives me a serious neck ache due to the design; otherwise it would have been perfect for me.. NOTE: Amazon is combining reviews for several different types of aprons, so please be aware that this review is for the cotton denim apron being sold.

Utterly disastrous poached eggs; this gets an F minus from me. I cannot believe I have to pay for this. This is not worth more than 50 cents.

This comes in three pieces. The yellow silicone cover on the handle, the frame itself with the egg well, and the silicone "bowl or rim." 

After washing for first use, submerge this poacher in boiling water up to rim of poacher and pour egg from a prep bowl into the egg well once the water begins to swirl. Cook for 2-4 minutes, drain, and serve.

It seems easy (see first four photos for instructions) but it is not.  First of all, when the water was ready, I poured the egg into the poacher and after a few seconds white foam (from the egg white) coagulated in the water. Once the egg was cooked, I gently lifted this from the pot. However, the yellow silicone handle kept sliding off so I had to keep re-attaching it. I finally squeezed it tightly while lifting the handle so it woud not fall off again. After the "egg well" drained as I lifted it from the pot, I turned over the poacher to release the egg.

Good luck. The egg is stuck relatively solid to the egg well. Only the yolk and top part of the egg white slipped out. I had to use a spoon to extricate the rest and it left some concrete residue behind.

I wanted to do another egg but the previous event clogged all the vents in the poacher.  It took me a couple of hours of soaking the poacher in Dawn Platinium and scrubbing it for about 15 minutes to remove the "concrete" residue. Not only was this a tremendous amout of work but it was not easy to remove the silicone rim from the poacher for washing and re-assembling.

In summary, this is an absolutely awful poacher. It would be best to just crack the egg into boiling water with vinegar and then removing it with a slotted spoon. I am glad I used a non-stick pan or I would have been scrubbing that into the wee hours.

THE VERDICT - This gets an F minus. Use only if you want to spend hours extracting one poached egg and working on the cleanup.

Barely does the job pitting cherries; although pits Bing cherries better. The purpose of this "industrial-sized" Leifheit cherry pitter is to be able to pit many cherries quickly without having to "reload" a cherry into the pitting chamber. I figured the need for a lot of pitted cherries when making pies or a large fruit salad would make such a gargantuan unit worthwhile. I already have the exceptionally designed and almost flawless [[ASIN:B000NQ925K OXO Good Grips Cherry Pitter]] but when this unit came became available, I felt it was worth trying out.

The unit comes with two rubber washers; one is a spare. What I had to do was remove the cardboard piece holding down the plunger arm and insert the rubber gasket into the slot. This gasket is needed to prevent the cherry pit from coming back into the cherry after I pulled up on the plunger. For my test, I tried to pit both the firmer Rainier cherries and the less firm Bing cherries with this cherry pitter. Even though the instructions do not mention pitting olives with this cherry stoner, I decided to try small black Kalamata olives as well--since my other cherry pitter can pit soft olives like this.

I loaded the Rainier cherries into the hopper and they didn't really line up in the pitting chamber; sometimes they had to be pushed into the hole for pitting. Once I pushed the plunger, I had to pull up fully to release the pitted cherry into the exit shoot. Of about 50 Rainer cherries I pitted many were damaged on the exit (partially squished or broken) and all but about 4 had the pits remain in the cherry. For the cherries that exited into the waiting bowl, I had to pry open the cherry to remove the pits. I then tried pitting about 50 sweet cherries and they pitted easier since they were softer cherries. However, I still had some squished cherries exit the hopper and about 6 of the cherries that exited had pits that had to be pulled out by hand. Since I also wanted to know if olives would work, I tried about 4 of them and found out quickly this unit cannot pit olives.

As I was washing the unit I noted that the washer was destroyed just from pitting these few cherries. It appears the plunger not only pitted my cherries but also chopped out part of the washer. When I inserted the washer, I made sure it was centered and that the pitter blade passed cleanly through the center of the washer's hole. However, with all the cherry pitting activity it probably moved around and caused large holes in the washer. Not only does this reduce the effectiveness of the pitting but I had to throw out the washer and put in the spare.

In summary, I cannot recommend this cherry pitter to anyone. The only redeeming quality it has are the rubber feet on the bottom of the unit that keeps the cherry pitter base firmly in place during pitting. Other than this, the unit is too huge. The pitting chamber so enormous compared to the hopper you put the cherries in. Also the plunger cannot be locked down for storage and stands at attention like a rocket about to take off. The pitter barely pits Bing cherries (the dark colored ones with a firm but softer flesh) and has a 95% failure rate when pitting Rainier cherries. I had high hopes for this cherry stoner and was sadly disappointed. I was going to give this unit 1 star but since it did pit the Bing cherries somewhat, I rated this 2 stars. I have not decided yet whether I'm going to send this to the recycling bin or keep it as a conversation piece, but I doubt I'll ever use this to pit cherries again.

This pepper mill needs improvement. This pepper mill is not only for wealthy consumers looking for another way to spend their money. It can be a medical aid in some cases for those with hand problems. I have no objection to a high-priced automatic pepper mill because those who have hand problems (arthritis, carpel tunnel, one arm or hand, etc.) will find it possible to now grind pepper and coriander without difficulty or pain. After all I purchased a $200 [[ASIN:B000A76VCY Breville 800CPXL Die-Cast Stainless-Steel Motorized Citrus Press]] just to reduce the hand stress I was experiencing with squeezing lemons and limes which I absolutely love and believe it was money well spent.

However, this pepper mill is not in the same league. I expected an elite "machine" that worked simply and well and here's what I got.

In the box is one large pepper mill that is mostly all motor. It comes with a small container of peppercorns and what looks like a square base on which the pepper mill should rest when not in use. (NOTE - It slips easily off this base if that is what it was designed for.) There are also 6 AAA batteries included.

The pepper mill has to be disassembled to load the peppercorns and also to extract the motor and load the batteries. Extracting the motor was incredibly cumbersome. There are 2 sliding levers on the inside plate that have to be shifted toward the inside of the motor with a pencil or file. In the process, my levers bent and almost broke off (so they are shoddy levers). Once the levers are no longer holding the motor in place, the unit has to be lightly shaken to dislodge the motor. It took a while for it to dislodge. Once the motor is removed, the batteries were easy to insert and the direction of insertion (negative and positive) were clearly marked.

After battery installation, I had to reverse the entire process. Inserting the motor is tricky as well as I had to line up certain parts, then push down the motor, and re-seat the levers out and under the base lip.

The top of the vessel holding the peppercorns that came with this product also acts also like funnel. I had to unscrew the top and punch out the center piece then lay this over the peppercorn reservoir to fill it. Once that was done. I screwed the holder to the base. (NOTE - Save the container that came with the peppercorns because it is a measuring cup for refilling the reservoir.)

As per the manual, only black, white, and green (dry) peppercorns of 5 mm (0.2") or less should be used in this mill for optimal performance. It also grinds pink peppercorns as long as the pink ones are no more than 15% of the peppercorns being ground. In addition, it grinds dry coriander seeds.

There are six (6) gradations of grind (from fine to coarse) marked on the bottom dial. Based on my tests (since the instructions are not clear on this), it appears the single horizontal line indicates a fine grind and as the lines increase in number to six (6) lines that indicates a coarser grind. The grind level is set by turning the dial to line up the desired grind lines with the letter P written on the reservoir (which is difficult to see).

To dispense the pepper, I just lightly touched the "button" on the top of the base to activate the motor. A light comes on and then dispenses the pepper according to the grind level set. The mill grinds quickly and well. Since the unit engages the motor easily, it means if one of my cats touches the top, the pepper will also grind.

In summary, had I paid for this product, I would have sent it back for a refund. The batteries are too difficult to get to, the levers holding the motor in place are poor quality and easily broken, there is no shutoff for the motor once the batteries are installed so the slightest touch of the button grinds pepper, and it does not feel like the elite "machine" I expected. Also, the lifetime warranty is on the motor only and no other part. If this grinder came with USB or other rechargeable and easy to insert batteries, had the ability to turn off the motor, felt like a quality kitchen tool, and the instructions were clearer (five languages follow each instruction) then I would have given this 5 stars. As it stands now, I consider this a working prototype only and not a kitchen tool that should be sold for such a high price.

Horrible canning experience; rims are "sticky"; golden lids don't seal; stick with Ball. This is a 40-pack set of mason jars with:
- 30 sliver lids with rims
- 10 golden lids with rims
- 1 tiny brush
- 40 chalkboard labels with chalk marker

I only ever used Ball jars, lids, and rims in the past and now I know why. I had an opportunity to try this and CANNOT recommend them.

I spent hours water bath canning only to discover that the golden lids DO NOT SEAL at all--that is 25% of the jars. In the fourth photo, the gold rim and lid is to the left of the picture. The silver lids appear to seal but the rims on about 90% of the jars are almost impossible to screw on. They are very sticky. After having the bad experience with the golden lids and using 14 of the jars with lids and rims, I decided to use my Ball canning set instead . When using a Ball rim, they glide on these jars. I have a funny feeling that because the rims are so bad, that the seal is broken periodically as a result of unscrewing the rim and checking if the lid is holding. Produces mild heat on highest setting; arrived with black smudges on top; initial use has heat smell. This deep pocket heated mattress pad for a king-sized bed is like a heating pad. There are two controls that plug in on the top of the mattress cover and have settings for warm, low, medium, and high heat. The warm setting is the default. I could not feel much heat from any of the settings except for the high setting. The high setting provided a very low and very nice warmth. There are two controls; one for each side of the bed. There is a slight heat smell during first use.

I have a king sized bed that has a tall mattress with a topper. I require 16" deep pockets and the pockets on this are large enough to handle that even though there is nothing on the packaging that says that. This cover works (longevity unknown) but the CONS make this a pass for me.

PROS
- It provides a nice light heat on the highest setting that apparently shuts off after 10 hours. I did not test the 10-hour shutoff as I'm rarely in bed for more than 6 hours.

- There are two controls for both sides of the bed so the other bed partner can select a different heat setting.

- The mattress pad is attractive and comfortable to lay on (except for the area with the plugs).

- It has deep pockets for a tall king-size mattress and fits up to my mattress pocket size of 16".

CONS
- The electrical connection should have been located on the headboard side of the pad and only on the rim (meaning pocket side) of the pad. Currently, the connection is located at the foot of the mattress pad (based on the label). Of course, I can turn the label upside down and face the connection toward the top (which is what I did to access an electric socket); however, the plug on both sides is on the top and can be felt as a lump if laying down in that area.

- The pad I received arrived with black smudges as if someone walked on the mattress pad. When I order a new product, I expect to receive it in pristine condition.

- There was some cotton sticking out of the trim (see photo). This is a minor detail and can just be cut off, but it is another sign of sloppiness.

- Although the elastic section (pockets) fit over my mattress, the elastic is not gripping enough. This means, it is easy for the mattress pad to slide off the mattress unless I sandwich the remaining cloth between the mattress and the box spring.

- There is a bit of a heat smell during first use; not much but is to be expected.

- This unit has to be unplugged daily as there is no shutoff except for the claim that it shuts off after 10 hours, which I did not test.

- I would not count on being able to wash this successfully. It says I can wash this in a machine for 5 min but I personally wouldn't do that. I would suggest spot cleaning if needed.

In summary, this mattress pad works to produce very low heat on the highest setting. It will fit a king-sized bed with 16" to perhaps 17" deep pockets but the elastic is too loose to keep it on the bed unless it is wedged between the mattress and box spring. The location of the plugs is a problem and the dirty topper I received is an utter disappointment. The current price of $33.99 ($39.99 minus 15%) is very reasonable for this. A mattress pad without any heat for a king-sized bed is usually priced much higher. My recommendation is to pass on this pad and buy flannel sheets for the winter that keep one warm and toasty under the blankets. If a heated mattress pad is desired, I would say to look elsewhere.

text:
SUPER CHEAPO. You get what you pay for. Sadly in this case, it's even less. I missed the part that described this a COMPLETELY particle board with a cardboard back. (That's right, I thought it was packing. Nope, the folded cardboard in the packing mix was to be used as the backing of the dresser). The laminate paper is SO thin that if just look at too long it will rub off. Honestly, If I hadn't had to destroy the box to get it out (SUPER HEAVY) I would have just returned it. I think the seller is hoping you won't. Good thing Amazon backs up what they sell.

PROS:
*It was packaged about as well as I have ever seen. The edges were super reinforced. I've never seen such a well packaged cardboard box. (Having said that, the top piece was still broken in several places - sigh)
*It was packaged securely inside as well.
*I am 53, female. Put it together, by myself, in about 4 hours.
*Most of the pre-drilled areas were correcting drilled.
*Had all of the screws/parts needed, but see below..
*It's stylish... sort of retro looking to me.
*Honestly, it looked like a daunting task. But once started, it went fairly quickly.
*Ording from Amazon. They (Amazon) are SUPER good at coming up with solutions.

CONS:
*Upon taking inventory of all the misc screws and parts, I discovered one of the carpentry screws was broken. Sadly, the local hardware store did not carry them. Neither did the local furniture store. Contacted the manufacturer, NO RETURN CALL.
*NO SELLER CUSTOMER SERVICE AT ALL. Calling the 800 number gets you voice mail that they apparently don't ever pick up or return.
*This is such a cheap piece of furniture, it's hard to believe they could sell them for more than a $100. I will use it only temporarily and then it will likely go to the dump.
*The directions have NO written instructions. Pictures are good but did NOT help with the screws that were different than those packed WITH the handles. Eventually I sorted it out. But printed instructions would have helped there.
*As cheap as this dresser is, I was really disappointed to see that one of the drawer liner laminate was "flawed" right in the center. I put that drawer on the bottom row, but it is still an eyesore.
*The top was broken is several places, three showing on the top piece of the dresser. Again, I attempted to contact the seller thinking I might be able to purchase or obtain a new top piece. Seller does NOT RETURN PHONE CALLS OR ANY CONTACT.
*Smell. It smells like the chemicals used in making particle boarding. I believe there is a study that says those chemicals are harmful. Another reason it will most likely end up in the dump.

If you're still thinking you might try it, here's what you will need to make it easier:
A small hammer, a cordless drill (that you can easily control), a flat head and phillips screw driver. About 4-5 hours, maybe less if you have a second set of hands.
Optional: A shot of whiskey for the frustration factor.

Hope this is helpful in some way.

UPDATE: 5/18 Dresser on the way to the dump. Purchased a very nice drawer, on sale, at the local furniture store. Can't say I'm sad to see it go. I think the lesson here is that in regards to furniture, perhaps it's better to purchase locally so you can actually see and approve of what you're getting. Happy shopping!

A couple of hints... don't tighten all the screws after placing the side pieces until you have all them placed, even though the directions show you doing this, as it will be next to impossible to fit the last piece if you've tightened the screws prior. Also, I would wear gloves when placing the wooden slats as they are smooth on the wide edge, but extremely rough and splintery on the edges. The instruction booklet page is fairly easy to read with graphics, as you can see in the photos I provided.

text:
Our Bad Tasting Water is Still Bad...No Improvement While Using the Brita Pitcher. 10 years ago, we moved into a new home. At our old home, we had the BEST tap water ever. There was absolutely no need for us to buy bottled water, our tap water was that good and refreshing. At our new and current home, we had a different water provider. Gone was our delicious tap water. It was replaced with awful tasting water. Our home has a whole home water softener. But its a waste. It doesn't help at all. Our tap water is still awful. It leaves blue-green rings in the toilet bowl, bathtub and on the dishes back when we still used the dishwasher. (Dishwasher broke, never replaced it as I don't mind doing dishes by hand) Of course the water company says the water is at an acceptable quality. Less than two years after we moved into this home, our normally healthy dog got terribly sick and had to be put to sleep . He was in full kidney failure. He never had any problems before. We've gone through 3 hot water heaters in the 10 years that we've lived here. When we moved to this home, we brought our almost 3 year old washing machine along. It stopped working less than 2 years after moving here. All of these things could, of course, be coincidence. But its my belief all of these things are due to our terrible water. Weeks after we lost our dog, a spring water stand was built close to our home. From that moment on, we completely stopped using tap water for drinking/cooking and began to use ONLY spring water. (Still had to use tap water to bathe, etc) And we only give our pets spring water to drink as well.

I was anxious to try the Brita pitcher. I hoped that it would make our tap water taste better and we'd be able to drink it. I had no problems whatsoever with the pitcher, it was easy to use. Panasonic residential-level microwave ovens are a good choice only if you want to replace your oven frequently. All of the very wonderful features of this oven end up meaning nothing, because the door latch is junky and destined to fail early. (Planned obsolescence?)

After spending hours researching other residential microwave brands and finding other serious problems relating to durability, and after learning that literally 50% of residential microwaves, regardless of the brand, are made in just one factory in China -- with virtually identical or identical internal parts -- I have moved on to commercial grade. The ordinary pull handle on most commercial models is much more reliable than a push-button system. A commercial grade microwave will not have all of the bells and whistles of a residential model, but it will be built for durability, and you can get a good one for $250 - 325.

After numerous bad experiences with residential models failing way too soon, durability is all I care about at this point.

The two main reasons I am giving this just 2 stars - and they are important reasons! - are: #1 - the holes are drilled in the wrong places on the legs to the headboard. You cannot install the cross bar AND the sides to the frame - the holes are simply in the wrong places to do both. Of course we chose to install the sides to the frame, since we're not actually placing any weight on this headboard and frame. But if we were, I would be livid, since the center supports rely on being screwed to the crossbar to support the slats, and ultimately, a bed. I mean, this would be completely USELESS as it was sent to me for use as a bed. Reason #2 - nearly every hinge where I needed to connect pieces was totally bent. I needed to use a clamp and a lot of muscle so I could straighten the hinges and screw them flush to the other part of the frame. Assembly was SUCH a frustrating experience because it was just poorly made. Shame on the manufacturer.
